final_rationale: The verdict remains suspicious because the Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and, in several respects, conceded the core concern. That narrower framing matters, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here. A caveated-compliance outcome would require evidence that the caveat itself is operationalized in a policy-satisfying way: resolution of the gap, an actual disclosure artifact, or approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record still shows a 1.2-point miss in an advertising policy review segment tied to two named rollout commitments, an open legal ticket on disclosure, and a policy requiring disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Because that compliance predicate remains unresolved on the current evidence, the position is still only partly supported and remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the segment gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible disclosure artifact was provided showing the limitation is actually disclosed for the named launch use case.
No approved risk acceptance was provided.
Legal review remains open on whether disclosure is required.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one incidents support overall readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure predicate for a named launch use case.
